ordered_diagnoses: Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of asymptomatic cutaneous eruption with progressive enlargement of lesions
salient_findings: Multiple papules and plaques with central depression on the dorsal forearms and nape of the neck
Dense inflammatory neutrophilic infiltrate within the dermis and marked dermal edema on biopsy
key_facts: 45-year-old man
5-day history of cutaneous eruption
Asymptomatic
No fever, malaise, or other constitutional symptoms
No contact with cattle or sheep
No medications
No significant medical history
Lesions began small and progressively enlarged
Gram stain of fluid from one lesion was inconclusive
Punch biopsy showed no epidermal changes
White-cell count of 13,000/mm3 with 89% neutrophils
Normal peripheral smear
Renal and liver function tests were within normal limits
Imaging of the abdomen and pelvis was unremarkable
Urine testing for Bence–Jones protein was negative

shortlist: Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of asymptomatic cutaneous eruption with progressive enlargement of lesions and dense inflammatory neutrophilic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Lesions began small and progressively enlarged with a striking central depression

shortlist.label: Erythema elevatum diutinum
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic cutaneous eruption with firm and nontender lesions

shortlist.label: Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands
shortlist.why_kept: Dense inflammatory neutrophilic infiltrate within the dermis and lesions on the dorsal forearms

shortlist.label: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: White-cell count of 13,000/mm3 with 89% neutrophils and acute onset of cutaneous eruption

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of an abrupt onset of asymptomatic cutaneous eruption with lesions showing a striking central depression, a dense inflammatory neutrophilic infiltrate within the dermis, and a high white-cell count with 89% neutrophils are consistent with Sweet syndrome.

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: Typically presents with painful ulcers, which is not consistent with the patient's asymptomatic lesions.

rejected.label: Erythema elevatum diutinum
rejected.why: Characterized by chronic or recurrent lesions, which does not match the patient's acute 5-day history.

rejected.label: Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands
rejected.why: Specifically affects the hands, whereas the patient's lesions are on the neck and forearms.

rejected.label: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis
rejected.why: The patient does not have fever, which is a key component of this condition.
